title: Historical Metrics — Proof of Correctness

timezone.storedConvention: UTC wall-clock value written into a naive column
timezone.reportingConvention: reporting period boundaries converted to WIB; DB values treated as UTC
timezone.snapshotBusinessDateConvention: DailyBusinessSnapshot.businessDate stores the UTC midnight of the WIB calendar day
timezone.verifiedBy: information_schema.columns data_type check (User, Transaksi, XPTransaction, PlayerActivity, GameResult, ProgresKompetensi, TestSession, DailyBusinessSnapshot)

metricInventory.windowFloor: User.createdAt >= 2026-06-28 (Supabase migration; pre-migration history not retained)
metricInventory.note: User.createdAt is an immutable event-like field (set once at creation), but only reconstructable after the Supabase migration that re-created accounts.
DAU is proxied by distinct users writing XP activity. It is an INFERENCE (XP is a proxy for 'active'), and only valid from 2026-08-03 when XPTransaction began.

metricInventory.source: XPTransaction.createdAt (distinct userId per trailing 7 WIB days)
metricInventory.note: Same XP proxy + window caveat as DAU.

metricInventory.source: XPTransaction.createdAt (distinct userId per trailing 30 WIB days)
metricInventory.note: Same XP proxy + window caveat as DAU. MAU before 2026-08-03 is unreconstructable.

Cohort membership reconstructable from User.createdAt, but D7/D30 activity can only be measured from 2026-08-03. Early cohorts have no valid activity signal. Timestamp existence alone does NOT prove retention.
Cash collected is an append-only ledger of SUCCESS transactions and IS reconstructable. However it is CASH, not MRR — the two must never be equated.

MRR is a composition of ACTIVE premium subscribers at a point in time. It relies on mutable current-state fields (isPremium, premiumUntil, premiumPlan) + a live join to latest SUCCESS transaction. Past MRR values are lost — cannot be reconstructed historically. Only a daily snapshot preserves it.
murid/guru × monthly/yearly MRR decomposition has the same mutable-current-state dependency; history lost without a snapshot.
Count of active premium users at a past moment is unreconstructable — only the current isPremium/premiumUntil state survives; expiry/churn history is not retained as a ledger.
murid vs guru premium split at a past moment depends on mutable role + premium state; role is not ledgered.
Trial-active count relies on the mutable trialEndsAt of the latest state; expired trial history is not retained.
Karya published per day is append-only and reconstructable from 2026-07-09.
Simulation sessions started per day is append-only and reconstructable from 2026-07-07.
Unit completions are append-only event-like rows, reconstructable from 2026-06-29.
XP awarded per source per day is a ledger and reconstructable from 2026-08-03 (modern engine). Legacy XpLedger starts 2026-07-28 but is a different engine.

metricInventory.source: NOT reconstructable (role is mutable, no role-change ledger)
metricInventory.note: Role-based growth history is corruptible because User.role is a mutable field overwritten over time (e.g., founder/role migrations). Current role distribution is a FACT, but historical role-based growth is NOT reconstructable.

metricInventory.source: NOT reconstructable (dead VPS, no retained canonical timestamps)
metricInventory.note: All product activity before the Supabase migration (pre-2026-06-28) is not retained in the canonical store. This is genuinely UNKNOWN and must never be estimated.

classificationChecks.rule1: Mutable current-state fields (isPremium/premiumUntil/premiumPlan/role/xp/lastActiveAt) are never treated as historical truth.
classificationChecks.rule3: Timestamp existence alone does not prove retention validity.
classificationChecks.rule4: Role changes corrupt historical role-based growth; role is not ledgered.
classificationChecks.rule5: UNKNOWN is never converted into an estimate.

reconciliation.method: Live recompute of MRR (non-founder active premium, plan from latest SUCCESS transaksi) vs latest DailyBusinessSnapshot.mrr
reconciliation.interpretation: Snapshot MRR formula is internally consistent with an independent live recompute using the SAME canonical formula.

liveFacts.note: Live facts are populated only when the read-only DB connection was available, else null/unavailable.

architectureVerdict: Evidence-driven hybrid is REQUIRED, not merely convenient: MRR and premium state are provably NOT reconstructable from retained data (mutable current-state only), while user/engagement/content/learning metrics ARE reconstructable from event ledgers — but only within their recorded windows. Hence: keep append-only DailyBusinessSnapshot for MRR/premium (core snapshot data), and derive reconstructable engagement metrics from primary event tables (facts) rather than materializing them.
backfillVerdict: No historical backfill is possible for MRR or premium state before the snapshot's start (2026-09-02): the underlying point-in-time active-subscriber composition does not exist for earlier dates. Do NOT backfill MRR/premium; snapshot from now forward. For reconstructable engagement metrics, backfill from primary tables is possible but only for the recorded window (floors listed per metric).
